verses.text: Di word of di Lord wey come to Joel, Pethuel pikin.
Hear dis, una old men, and give ear, all una inhabitants of di land. Dis don happen for una days, or for di days of una fathers?
Tell una children about am, and make una children tell dem children, and dem children another generation.
Dat wey di swarming locust leave, di great locust don eat. Dat wey di great locust leave, di young locust don eat. Dat wey di young locust leave, di caterpillar don eat.
Awake, una drunkards, and weep! Wail, all una wine drinkers, because of di sweet wine, because e dey cut off from una mouth.
Because nation don come up on my land, strong, and without number. Im teeth na lion teeth, and e get fangs of lioness.
E don lay my vine waste, and strip my fig tree. E don strip am bare, and throw am away. Im branches dey made white.
Mourn like virgin wey dey clothed with sackcloth for di husband of her youth.
Di meal offering and di drink offering dey cut off from di house of di Lord. Di priests, di Lord ministers, mourn.
Di field dey ruined. Di ground mourn, because di grain dey destroyed. Di new wine dey dried up. Di oil languish.
Dey ashamed, una farmers. Howl, una vinedressers, for di wheat and for di barley, because di harvest of di field don perish.

Di vine dey dried up, and di fig tree languish. Di pomegranate tree, di palm tree also, and di apple tree, even all di trees of di field, dey withered, because joy dey withered away from di sons of men.

Gird yourselves with sackcloth, and lament, una priests. Wail, una ministers of di altar. Come, lie all night in sackcloth, una ministers of my God, because di meal offering and di drink offering dey withheld from di house of your God.
Sanctify fast. Call solemn assembly. Gather di elders and all di inhabitants of di land to di house of di Lord your God, and cry to di Lord.
Alas for di day! Because di day of di Lord dey at hand, and e go come as destruction from di Almighty.
No be say di food dey cut off before our eyes, joy and gladness from di house of our God?
Di seeds shrivel under dem clods. Di granaries dey desolate. Di barns dey broken down, because di grain don dry up.
How di animals groan! Di herds of livestock dey perplexed, because dem no get pasture. Yes, di flocks of sheep dey made desolate.
Di Lord, I cry to you, because di fire don devour di pastures of di wilderness, and di flame don burn all di trees of di field.
Yes, di animals of di field pant to you, because di water brooks dey dried up, and di fire don devour di pastures of di wilderness.
Blow di trumpet for Zion, and sound di alarm for my holy mountain. Make all di inhabitants of di land tremble, because di day of di Lord dey come. E dey near,

day of darkness and gloom, day of clouds and thick darkness. As di dawn spread on di mountains, great and strong people dey. Nothing dey like dem before, neither go dey any more after dem, even to di years of many generations.
Fire devour before dem, and behind dem flame dey burn. Di land dey like di garden of Eden before dem, and behind dem desolate wilderness. Yes, and nothing escape dem.
Dem appearance dey like di appearance of horses. Like horsemen, so dem dey run.
Like di noise of chariots, dem leap on di tops of di mountains, like di noise of flame of fire wey devour stubble, like strong people set in battle array.
Before dem di peoples dey in anguish. All faces gather blackness.
Dem run like mighty men. Dem climb di wall like men of war. Dem march everyone on im ways, and dem no break dem ranks.
Dem no jostle one another. Dem march everyone in im path. Dem burst through di weapons, and no dey broken.
Dem rush on di city. Dem run on di wall. Dem climb up into di houses. Dem enter in at di windows like thief.
Di earth quake before dem. Di heavens tremble. Di sun and di moon dey darkened, and di stars withdraw dem shining.
Di Lord utter im voice before im army, because im forces dey very great, because dem wey execute im word dey strong, because di day of di Lord dey great and very awesome. Who fit endure am?
“Yet even now,” talk di Lord, “turn to me with all your heart, and with fasting, and with weeping, and with mourning.
Tear your heart, and no tear your garments, and return to di Lord your God, because e dey gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness, and e relent of evil.
Who know whether e no go turn and relent, and leave blessing behind am, even meal offering and drink offering to di Lord your God?”
Blow di trumpet for Zion! Sanctify fast. Call solemn assembly.
Gather di people. Sanctify di assembly. Assemble di elders. Gather di children, and dem wey nurse at breasts. Make di bridegroom go forth from im room, and di bride out of her chamber.

Make di priests, di ministers of di Lord, weep between di porch and di altar, and make dem talk, ‘Spare your people, di Lord, and no give your heritage to reproach, say di nations rule over dem. Why dem go talk among di peoples, “Where dem God dey?”’
Den di Lord go dey jealous for im land, and have pity on im people.
Di Lord go answer and talk to im people, ‘See, I go send una grain, and new wine, and oil, and una go dey satisfied with am. I no go make una reproach among di nations any more.

But I go remove far from una di northern army, and go drive am into barren and desolate land, im face toward di eastern sea, and im end toward di western sea. Im stench go come up, and im stink go rise, because e don do great things.’
No fear, land. Dey glad and rejoice, because di Lord don do great things.
No dey afraid, una animals of di field, because di pastures of di wilderness spring up, because di tree bear im fruit. Di fig tree and di vine yield dem strength.

Dey glad then, una children of Zion, and rejoice for di Lord una God, because e give una di former rain in right measure, and e cause di rain to come down for una, di former rain and di latter rain, as before.
Di threshing floors go dey full of grain, and di vats go overflow with new wine and oil.
I go restore to una di years wey di swarming locust don eat, di great locust, and di young locust, and di caterpillar, my great army wey I send among una.
Una go eat plenty and dey satisfied, and praise di name of di Lord una God, wey don deal wondrously with una. My people go never dey ashamed.
Una go know say I dey for di middle of Israel, and say I be di Lord una God, and none other. My people go never dey ashamed.
E go happen afterward, say I go pour out my Spirit on all flesh. Una sons and una daughters go prophesy. Una old men go dream dreams. Una young men go see visions.
Also on di servants and on di servant girls for dose days I go pour out my Spirit.
I go show wonders for di heavens and for di earth: blood, and fire, and pillars of smoke.
Di sun go dey turned into darkness, and di moon into blood, before di great and awesome day of di Lord come.

E go happen say everyone wey call on di name of di Lord go dey saved, because for Mount Zion and for Jerusalem go dey those wey escape, as di Lord don talk, and among di remnant dem wey di Lord go call.
“For, see, for dose days, and for dat time, when I go restore di fortunes of Judah and Jerusalem,

I go gather all di nations, and go bring dem down into di valley of Jehoshaphat. I go enter into judgment with dem dere for my people, and for my heritage Israel, wey dem don scatter among di nations, and divide up my land.
Dem don cast lots for my people, and don give boy for prostitute, and sell girl for wine, so that dem go drink.

Yes, and wetin una get to do with me, Tyre, and Sidon, and all di regions of Philistia? Una go render me recompense? If una recompense me, I go swiftly and speedily return una recompense on una own head.
Because una don take my silver and my gold, and don carry into una temples my goodly pleasant things.
Una don sell di children of Judah and di children of Jerusalem to di Greeks, so that una go remove dem far from dem border.
See, I go stir dem up out of di place where una don sell dem, and I go return una recompense on una own head.
I go sell una sons and una daughters into di hand of di children of Judah, and dem go sell dem to di Sabeans, to nation far off, because di Lord don speak am.”
Proclaim dis among di nations: Prepare war. Stir up di mighty men. Make all di men of war draw near. Make dem come up.
Beat una plowshares into swords, and una pruning hooks into spears. Make di weak talk, “I dey strong.”
Hurry, and come, all una nations round about, and gather yourselves together. Cause your mighty ones to come down dere, di Lord.
Make di nations dey stirred up, and come up to di valley of Jehoshaphat, because dere I go sit to judge all di nations round about.
Put in di sickle, because di harvest dey ripe. Come, tread, because di winepress dey full. Di vats overflow, because dem wickedness dey great.
Multitudes, multitudes dey for di valley of decision, because di day of di Lord dey near for di valley of decision.
Di sun and di moon dey darkened, and di stars withdraw dem shining.
Di Lord go roar from Zion, and utter im voice from Jerusalem. Di heavens and di earth go shake, but di Lord go be refuge to im people, and stronghold to di children of Israel.
“So una go know say I be di Lord una God, dwelling for Zion, my holy mountain. Den Jerusalem go be holy, and strangers go pass through her no more.

E go happen for dat day say di mountains go drip sweet wine, and di hills go flow with milk, and all di brooks of Judah go flow with water. Spring go come out of di house of di Lord, and go water di valley of Shittim.
Egypt go be desolation, and Edom go be desolate wilderness, for di violence against di children of Judah, because dem don shed innocent blood for dem land.
But Judah go dwell forever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation.
I go cleanse dem of dem blood wey I no yet cleanse, because di Lord dwell for Zion.”
